units.RK-10.1-073: That no room-state write follows the commit's transaction is the shape of the store's writes: a scenario sees the timeline and the counters agree after every call, which RK-10.1-070 and RK-10.1-071 cover, never a write made apart from the commit.
units.RK-10.1-135: The warning is a log line, and no step of a scenario reads the implementation's log; a scenario sees only that the key or stamp is dropped (RK-10.1-134), or kept when send_event passes it (RK-10.1-136).
units.RK-10.1-140: That the framework sets no timeout of its own is an absence a scenario cannot show: a delivery held at a gate shows only that nothing fired during the hold, and a runner fails any call held past its own bound.
units.RK-10.1.1-013: How a hook reads an instruction is the hook's own code, which only an integrator keeps: a scripted hook records its payload and interprets nothing, so a scenario sees only that the event is an instruction (RK-10.1.1-003) and that only the application issues one (RK-10.1.1-004).
units.RK-10.2-007: BroadcastResult is what the pipeline's own broadcast() returns: no public call hands it out, so a scenario reads its members only through the units that produce them (deliveries, reentry events, tasks, observations, per-channel errors).
units.RK-10.3-020: The unit binds an implementation that accepts another edit_source. Both implementations refuse any value but sender, system and null as the content is built, so the case never arises in a runner: a scenario that passes another value sees the build's refusal, never a check as the sender's.
units.RK-10.6-009: The TurnBackend interface (submit, control, serve, close) is the shape of an object no step calls: its owner-side and executor-side messages lie below the public API a scenario drives (as for RK-10.6.3-009). What a scenario sees of its close, a turn still open given up as the kit's close closes its backend, and the delivery whose turn it was counting its cleanup done, is RK-10.6.8-025's and RK-10.6.8-026's, which scenarios cite; the reason backend_closed a turn link raises, the transport's release and the executor side's close are each implementation's own tests'.
units.RK-10.6.1-010: This sets what the backend does not carry and obliges nothing a scenario can see: a speech-to-speech channel's model holds the conversation in the owner's process, so it has no intelligence turn for a backend to carry, and the fan-out of an event to another process's live connections belongs to a deployment.
units.RK-10.6.1-011: The serialized messages a backend carries lie below the public API a scenario drives: no step reads or writes a link message, which a backend's own tests do. The same scenarios run on the in-memory and a distributed backend show only that the outcomes agree.
units.RK-10.6.1-012: Whether the in-memory backend serializes each message is not observable through the public API: a turn's output reads the same either way; what a scenario can see of it, an error rebuilt by its class, is RK-10.6.8-043's.
units.RK-10.6.1-013: That nothing changes a request's events in place is a property of the language objects the owner and the executor hold: no scripted hook or channel changes a record in place, and a hook's modify returns a new one.
units.RK-10.6.1-015: Whether an implementation keeps a local shortcut to the channel's objects is its internal structure: a scenario sees the turn's outcome, which a shortcut and the backend give alike.
units.RK-10.6.1-016: Holds of the suite as a whole, not of one scenario: every scenario of an intelligence channel runs through the in-memory backend, and their receipts are the evidence.
units.RK-10.6.2-006: ChannelDeclaration and AgentIdentity are the shape of the record a declaration carries: no step reads a declaration, which a runner builds from its setup. A scenario sees what the owner reads of one through the behaviour it drives, which RK-10.6.2-008, RK-10.6.2-010 and RK-10.6.2-011 state and scenarios cite: the declared channel found wherever a channel is looked up, its turns run on an executor that builds it, and its greeting read as the same channel registered live reads.
units.RK-10.6.3-001: The families of messages a backend carries lie below the public API a scenario drives: no step reads or writes a link message, which a backend's own tests do (as for RK-10.6.3-009).
units.RK-10.6.3-003: The frames and their members lie below the public API a scenario drives: no step reads a frame. A scenario sees what the owner makes of them, through the units of Sections 10.6.4, 10.6.5 and 10.6.8 that scenarios cite.
units.RK-10.6.3-004: The control messages and their members lie below the public API a scenario drives: no step reads a control message. A scenario sees their effects (a reader's pull, a cancel, a steer, an input answer) through the units of Sections 10.6.4, 10.6.5 and 10.6.8 that scenarios cite.
units.RK-10.6.3-006: The executor's calls on the owner (tool_call, call_cancel, host_call) lie below the public API: a scenario sees the tool or verb served on the owner and a withdrawn call cancelled, which RK-10.6.5-006, RK-10.6.5-008 and RK-10.6.5-012 state and scenarios cite.
units.RK-10.6.3-009: A turn link's sequence numbers lie below the public API a scenario drives: no step can reorder, duplicate or drop a link message, which a backend's own tests do.
units.RK-10.6.3-010: A turn link's messages lie below the public API a scenario drives: no step duplicates, drops or reorders a link message, which a backend's own tests do (as for RK-10.6.3-009).
units.RK-10.6.3-011: The channel control messages and their members lie below the public API: a scenario sees an attach, a detach, a release or a channel call take effect, which RK-10.6.3-013 to RK-10.6.3-018, RK-10.6.3-020, RK-10.6.3-021, RK-10.6.3-026 to RK-10.6.3-028 and RK-10.6.3-030 to RK-10.6.3-032 state and scenarios cite.
units.RK-10.6.3-029: How a backend answers a channel call lies below the public API a scenario drives: no step reads the exchange a result comes back on, which a backend's own tests do (as for RK-10.6.3-009).
units.RK-10.6.3-033: A message reaching an executor that closed after the owner chose it is a race between placement and close that no step can hold, so each implementation's own tests cover it; an executor closed before the call is never chosen (RK-10.6.7-024, RK-10.6.7-025).
units.RK-10.6.3-034: The room_call and room_publication messages and their members lie below the public API: a scenario sees work a turn began act and publish after it, which RK-10.6.3-038 and RK-10.6.5-024 state and scenarios cite.
units.RK-10.6.4-002: That the owner builds its reader's ChannelOutput from the output frame lies below the public API: a scenario sees the turn's output, which reads the same whatever frame carried it.
units.RK-10.6.4-006: A pull's count and how the executor reads it lie below the public API a scenario drives: no step reads or writes a link message, which a backend's own tests do (as for RK-10.6.3-009).
units.RK-10.6.5-011: The members a tool_result carries lie below the public API: a scenario sees the answer the model reads and the call's outcome, which RK-10.6.5-006 and RK-10.6.5-008 state and scenarios cite.
units.RK-10.6.5-025: That each verb is one host_call with data arguments is the shape of the link below the public API, and documenting the set is the implementation's own; a scenario sees what the verbs do, which RK-10.6.5-026 states and scenarios cite.
units.RK-10.6.5-053: Whether a call or an answer carries the record fields lies below the public API: a scenario sees the turn's record, which reads the same for a call without the fields and one that changed nothing.
units.RK-10.6.5-055: What the in-memory backend carries beside the messages is its internal structure, which no step reads; a scenario sees the guards the carried context holds for the turn, which RK-10.6.5-054 states and scenarios cite.
units.RK-10.6.7-013: The owner never places a room's work on an executor that does not serve its organization (RK-10.6.7-010 to RK-10.6.7-012, which scenarios cite): only a backend's own tests can hand an executor such work, so its refusal is not reachable through the public API.
units.RK-10.6.7-015: That a declaration names no room is the shape of the record: a scenario sees the owner tie each room to the executor holding it, which RK-10.6.7-025 states and scenarios cite.
units.RK-10.6.7-019: Whether a turn crosses a transport or stays in the process lies below the public API: the turn's outcome reads the same either way, and the same scenarios run across a distributed backend show only that the outcomes agree.
units.RK-10.6.8-009: A turn busy with its CPU past heartbeat_timeout is a timing case no step makes: a scenario never blocks the runner's thread, and each implementation's own tests block it for real, roomkit's on its event loop, roomkit-rs's on one thread and on several.
units.RK-10.6.8-021: Only an executor whose cut lets the channel's code run on (Python's cancellation and finally) has a cleanup that a second message could interrupt; a roomkit-rs executor drops the cut work, its finalizers synchronous, so no fixture both runners build holds one between a close and a cancel. roomkit's tests/test_turns_control.py::test_a_close_after_a_cut_lets_the_channel_finish_its_cleanup and ::test_a_cut_after_a_close_lets_the_channel_finish_its_cleanup pin it.
units.RK-10.6.8-045: Declaring its error classes to the owner and to each executor is the host's own duty, which only an integrator keeps; a scenario sees the classes rebuilt, which RK-10.6.8-043 and RK-10.6.8-044 state and scenarios cite.
units.RK-10.6.8-049: Whether a side imports a module or runs its code to resolve a name is not observable through the public API: a scenario sees only the class an error comes back as (RK-10.6.8-047).
units.RK-10.6.9-004: This names as the owner's what other units and sections state (per-room order, RK-10.2-010; chain depth, Section 8.3; streamed segments, Section 10.6.4; the turn record, Sections 6.4 and 6.7): which side computes them is not observable.
units.RK-10.6.9-005: Holds of the suite as a whole, not of one scenario: whether an executor holds a store is how the host builds it, which no step sets, and every executors scenario runs on executors the runners build without one.
units.RK-10.6.9-006: The lock manager several owner processes share is a deployment prerequisite, and that an executor takes no room lock is its internal structure: a scenario sees the owner's lock rules, which the units of Section 13.5 state.
units.RK-5.14-002: Whether a ProtocolTrace can be changed once built is a property of the language object that holds it: no step of a scenario holds a trace object, and no call writes one.
units.RK-5.14-004: This paragraph points to Section 15.6, whose units state how traces are emitted, routed and buffered before a room exists. A scenario tests those units, never this pointer.
units.RK-5.2-011: A real channel's parse runs in no scenario: a scripted transport builds the runner's own source, and no step drives a provider's or a backend's input into an implementation's channel.
units.RK-5.5-040: The warning is a log line, and no step of a scenario reads the implementation's log; a scenario sees only that the reach does not fail (RK-5.5-039).
units.RK-5.7-021: The warning is a log line, and no step of a scenario reads the implementation's log; a scenario sees only how routing reads the value (RK-5.7-020).
units.RK-5.9-001: Channel.info is no record a step of a scenario reads, so no scenario can show the three levels kept apart; a scenario reads a binding's metadata through the units of Section 5.7, and a message's channel metadata as a custom router is given it (RK-10.4-009).
units.RK-7-001: This sentence frames Section 7: it names the three primitives that Sections 7.1 to 7.3 define and leaves their use to the integrator. A scenario tests a primitive through those units, which scenarios cite; the framing itself has no behaviour of its own to observe.
units.RK-9-001: These two sentences frame Section 9: they name hooks as the extensibility mechanism and what a hook can do to an event, which Sections 9.1 to 9.6 define. A scenario tests a hook through those units, which scenarios cite; the framing itself has no behaviour of its own to observe.
units.RK-9.2-005: This paragraph names which triggers an implementation must fire: those Section 26.1 lists for Level 0 and those each feature's section names. A scenario tests a trigger's firing through its row of the table and those sections' units, never through this pointer.
units.RK-9.2-055: ON_REALTIME_TOOL_CALL is Superseded: no implementation fires it, and the speech-to-speech tool call it named fires ON_TOOL_CALL (RK-9.2-073, Section 9.3), so no runner has a firing to observe.
units.RK-9.2-062: ON_CONSUMPTION is Planned: no implementation emits it yet, so no runner can observe it fire; its scenario comes with the capability (Section 8.5).
units.RK-9.2-084: ON_VIDEO_TRACK_ADDED is Planned: no implementation emits it yet, so no runner can observe it fire; its scenario comes with the capability.
units.RK-9.2-085: ON_VIDEO_TRACK_REMOVED is Planned: no implementation emits it yet, so no runner can observe it fire; its scenario comes with the capability.
units.RK-9.3-111: What a request object keeps exposing after settlement is a property of the language object the human-input handler returns: no step of a scenario holds that object, and the public reader (input_request) answers null once a request is settled.
units.RK-9.3-116: Giving a human-input handler as a plain tool handler is the integrator's wiring, which no step of a scenario makes: the implementation then serves an ordinary tool call, which the tool-call units cover.
units.RK-9.4-009: A MODIFY payload of another type than its trigger expects cannot be returned through a typed hook callback, and no scripted hook returns one (README, Reactions): the check is each implementation's own test, never a shared scenario's.
